propositions: Operator-attested evidence currently validates the existence of an attestation but lacks provenance context (environment, principal, privilege level, instrument type) needed to determine if the measurement could exhibit the failure being tested.

Two documented escapes occurred through undeclared provenance: measurements from account 579718921998/us-east-2 recorded as evidence for account 896586841071/us-east-1, and IAM permissions validated under broader privilege (bedrock:*) than production scope (bedrock:InvokeModel), making success meaningless.

Deterministic measurement-provenance fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) must be declared as indented continuation lines under [operator-attested] checkboxes in a single canonical form, with non-placeholder values and enum membership validated by a new det_measurement_provenance.py module.

An LLM-tier AGENT criterion project.measurement-provenance must compare declared environment against repository artifacts (e.g., Terraform backend), flag privilege_posture=broader on scoped-permission criteria, and distinguish live-call from simulation/static-analysis instruments—since simulators cannot detect runtime API behavior changes.

The contract amendment ships via project overlay (.rebar/criteria_routing.json) only, not the shipped default criteria set, so no cross-client behavior change occurs and pre-contract attestations are grandfathered with advisory-only surfacing.

Deterministic syntax and shape validation (presence, non-placeholder, enum membership) must pass without judgment of correctness, while semantic contradictions (declared vs. repo artifacts) and authorization-vs-instrument rules remain in the LLM criterion, maintaining the DET-first architecture.
